brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.requirement: Holder for the soldering iron while switched on and hot
requirements.evidence: Cover top at 1,0,0 (cover:1,0,0;full;top) with L-bracket accessory (accessory:0#1,0#1) and hook plate (accessory:0#1,0#0) provides a raised cradle/hook area to rest the iron off the bench. Configurator verifies geometry/mesh clearance only — it does not verify heat resistance, non-flammability or tip-temperature handling, so hot-use safety is unmet by the printed parts alone.

requirements.requirement: Two bins for solder and spare tips
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full (full-depth single compartment) and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (full-depth 2-compartment) provide two separate storage cells. Staged with solder-reel prop in bin:0,0,0; second bin available for tips/tweezers/small parts.

finish.summary: Compact 3-cell bench station: one cell capped with L-bracket + hook as iron cradle, two adjacent cells with full-depth bins for solder reel and tips. Geometry verified (meshClash clear, joints locked); heat/safety for a hot iron depends on user-chosen print material and is not verified.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
